ok_charon_s_gardens.blurb: Charon's Gardens occupies the far southwestern corner of the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge in Oklahoma, a rugged, maze-like landscape of granite where small outcrops can hide nearby features and finding the right cliff takes patience. Boulder problems and trad routes account for most of the climbing, with sport, top-rope and a little aid mixed in. Boulder grades are mostly V0 to V4, and roped routes run mostly 5.6 to 5.12, thickest around 5.9 to 5.11. The terrain includes slabs, domes, walls and cracks, and some of the rock is very crystalline. Climbing is possible all year, but cliffs facing south bake in summer, while shaded north faces stay cold in winter. Pear and Apple, Lost Dome, Crab Eyes and Steak Dinner are among the larger zones.

ma_central_ma.blurb: Central Massachusetts, around Worcester, is a boulderer's region first. Douglas State Forest has short cliff bands in its northern part and glacial erratics to the south and east; the granite there is frequently featureless, so expect slopers and tiny crimps. Rocky Pond, near Boylston, holds large erratics along the shore in gritty granite, with a wide mix of roofs, slabs, compression and mantels and hard problems up to V11. Most boulder problems fall between V0 and V4. Trad is concentrated at Crow Hill and the Leominster area north of Worcester, where routes span from about 5.5 to 5.12, and a small ice quarry there adds a handful of routes.

ca_mount_woodson.blurb: Mount Woodson is a boulder-covered promontory between Poway and Ramona in northern San Diego County, standing at about 1,800 feet. Hundreds of granodiorite boulders, weathered into rounded forms, are scattered over the mountain, which gives it a long reputation as a bouldering destination. The mix also includes plenty of trad, top-rope and a smaller number of sport routes, plus practice aid lines. Boulder problems cover everything from V0 to V11, while roped climbs are mainly short and run chiefly 5.10 to 5.12. Chalk shows which spots are most popular, and this is a heavily used, social area where you can watch as well as climb. Fry Koegel Trail, the Summit Area and the Poison Oak Boulder Area are among the larger zones.

co_telluride_norwood_area.blurb: The Telluride and Norwood area sits in the San Juan Mountains of southwest Colorado, with climbing around Ophir, Box Canyon and the Norwood end of the valley. Sport routes lead, followed by trad, with some boulders and a good number of ice climbs from WI3 to WI5. Most rock routes fall between 5.9 and 5.12. The rock changes by area: Ophir is built on a diorite and rhyolite mix close to granite and holds old-school multi-pitch trad plus some bolts; the Falls Walls and Pipeline Wall are bolted conglomerate pocket pulling; Mill Creek and the Ilium boulders are sandstone. Loose rock is a real concern, so test holds and wear a helmet. Some crags are sunny and others shaded, and climbing is possible year-round.

co_bank_the.blurb: The Bank is one of the sport-climbing sectors of Shelf Road, a limestone cliff area north of Cañon City, Colorado. Nearly all of its climbing is bolted, with just a few trad lines and a small number of boulders. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, and 5.10 and 5.11 carry the most routes, so it suits climbers working through the middle grades. The rock is vertical limestone, and the wider Shelf Road area is popular outside the summer months. Quarry Wall, Cactus Rose Cliff and Piggy Bank hold the largest numbers of routes.
